reading.title: Two Friends
reading.text: Sofia and Lena have been friends since they were five. They are childhood friends who grew up on the same street. When Sofia's family moved to another city, the girls were afraid they would lose touch. But they kept in touch by writing long letters and later by video calls. Once they fell out over a small mistake, but they made up in a few days. Sofia says a true friend is someone who stays with you in good times and bad times. This summer Lena will visit her.

reading.title: The Two Neighbours
reading.text: In our street there lived two neighbours, Mr Hadi and Mr Omar. For many years they were enemies because of a small fence between their gardens. They did not talk, and each gave the other a hostile look. One winter, a big storm broke both fences. Now they had a common enemy: the weather. They worked together to repair the damage. After a week, Mr Hadi brought tea, and the two men laughed together. The neighbours learned that it is better to forgive and forget than to make enemies.

listening.title: A School Rivalry
listening.script: Our class and the class next door are great rivals in sport. Last year they won the football match, and we won the running race. Some students say the other class is our enemy, but our teacher disagrees. She says a rival makes us work harder. She also says it is easy to make enemies with unkind words, but hard to make friends again. So before each match, the two teams now shake hands. This year we hope to defeat them, but we will still be friends afterwards.

reading.title: A Village Wedding
reading.text: Last Saturday, my cousin Nodir got married to a girl called Dilfuza. They had been engaged for six months. The wedding ceremony took place in our village, and more than two hundred guests attended. The bride wore a beautiful white dress, and the groom wore a dark suit and a wedding ring. There was music, dancing and a lot of delicious food. Everyone wished the married couple a long and happy marriage. After the wedding, they went on honeymoon to the lake for a week.

reading.text: Last year, Emma's parents decided to get a divorce. At first, Emma felt sad and confused. Her mother and father lived apart, and Emma stayed with her mother during the week. They share custody of the children, so Emma spends weekends with her father. Her teacher spoke to her kindly, and her friends listened to her. After a few months, Emma started to cope with the change. She says that her parents are not a couple any more, but they are still her parents, and they love her.

reading.title: Respect at School
reading.text: Our school has a simple rule: show respect for everyone. We treat teachers, cleaners and classmates with respect. If a student speaks in a rude way, he has to say sorry. Our head teacher says respect must be earned, but it should also be given. When we disagree, we respect each other's opinions and listen carefully. In many respects, this rule makes our school a calm place. I have great respect for our history teacher, because he is patient and fair. I hope every school will have such a rule.

reading.title: My Big Family
reading.text: I come from a big, close family. Besides my parents and two sisters, my grandparents live with us, so we are an extended family. On Fridays, we all get together for dinner, and relatives often visit. Music runs in the family: my grandfather plays the dutar, and I take after him. Last month, we made a family tree for a school project. I learned about distant relatives I had never met. My mother says family life is not always easy, but our family values are respect and love.
